platform.description: The registered client platform: android, ios, web, or unknown.
platform.value_set_source: read from data at run time (SELECT DISTINCT); no value list is declared

region.description: Derived region: Americas (US, BR), EMEA (GB, DE, FR), APAC (PH, ID, IN).
region.value_set_source: read from data at run time (SELECT DISTINCT); no value list is declared

channel.description: The acquisition channel of the account. content_seo is content marketing and SEO; organic is organic; paid_search is paid search; partnerships is an internal test integration; referral is referrals.
channel.value_set_source: read from data at run time (SELECT DISTINCT); no value list is declared

country.description: The account country, as an ISO code: US (the United States); BR (Brazil); GB (the United Kingdom); DE (Germany); FR (France); PH (the Philippines); ID (Indonesia); IN (India).
country.value_set_source: read from data at run time (SELECT DISTINCT); no value list is declared

is_internal.description: TRUE for staff and test accounts. Customer-facing figures exclude these (is_internal = false); the two governed active-user definitions differ only on whether they apply this filter.
is_internal.value_set_source: read from data at run time (SELECT DISTINCT); no value list is declared

trend_granularity.when: a time series is requested (group_by includes metric_time) but no bucket is grounded
trend_granularity.rationale: A trend needs enough points to show its shape and few enough to read: 15-40. Day is usually too granular, month too coarse over a short span; the rule computes the fit from the span rather than guessing. A bucket that crosses the period's edge reports data from outside the period, so only grains whose buckets line up with the period are considered.

canonical_segments.when: an unspecified breakdown is asked ('by segment') with no dimension named
canonical_segments.disclose: broken down by the standard business segments: platform (product), region (sales), channel (marketing)
canonical_segments.rationale: A senior analyst's first-pass breakdown is the canonical high-level business segments, not one arbitrary dimension. Showing all three is the analysis; it is not a fork worth a clarify.
